From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>

Subject: CarePilot discovery — acceptance of what we store and TTLs

Hi Amit / Jamie — great to meet you on the demo earlier. Quick recap of the data handling items we discussed and the asks you made. I want to confirm the specifics so we can keep your security/compliance folks aligned.

High-level commitments we discussed (please flag any corrections):
- Prompt inputs: accepted via API; default behavior is not stored persistently unless customer-enabled.
- Generated outputs: by default ephemeral for session-based flows (24-hour cache), persisted only if you call the ‘archive’ API or enable logging.
- Audit logs / request metadata (timestamps, model, token counts): retained for 90 days by default; can be extended with a Dedicated/Private contract.
- PII redaction: we offer automated redaction hooks and a manual review export for logged outputs.
- Data residency: hosted region = us-west; we can commit to us-only storage for your org under Dedicated/Private.

Action items for CarePilot to confirm:
1) Are you comfortable with a 24-hour ephemeral cache for session KV unless we explicitly persist?
2) Do you require that any outputs containing user PII be automatically redacted prior to storage? If yes, what fields are considered PII for you?
3) Who on your side will need the retention matrix and evidence (SOC2 artifacts, sample audit logs)?

Attachments: I’ve attached a first-pass retention_matrix_v1.xlsx and the call recording. The matrix maps "what we store" (prompts, outputs, logs, caches) to storage location and TTL. I’ll loop Security internally if you want a formal signed commitment.

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm questions 1–3 above by EOD Wednesday.
- We’ll send a security-ready doc with explicit TTL values and an example access-control policy.

Thanks,
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0128

Thanks Rishi — good summary. A few clarifications from our side:

1) 24-hour ephemeral cache works for most user session flows, but our clinical QA pipeline will persist outputs for 30 days for review. We need that to be configurable per route.
2) We need automatic redaction on outputs: at minimum email, SSN, and MRN (medical record number) fields. We can provide a sample schema.
3) Evidence: please share the retention matrix and sample audit log entries. Our InfoSec will want a sample export showing token-level counts and request IDs.

One more ask: does your hosted logging show full prompt text in audit exports? If yes, we need a way to redact that in the export or opt-out per-tenant.

Best,
Amit Shah
CTO, CarePilot
amit@carepilot.ai

Hi Amit / Jamie —

Thanks for the clear asks. Below are the formal answers and the next steps from Security/Privacy. Please consider this our standard hosted behavior; we can lock commitments into Dedicated/Private contracts if you need contractual guarantees.

1) Per-route TTLs
- Default session cache TTL: 24 hours (applies to KV cache and temporary output caching).
- Configurable per-route TTL: we can set a longer TTL for specific endpoints (e.g., clinical QA route) up to 90 days; you requested 30 days and we confirm we can configure that per-route via the Redwood Console policies.

2) Automatic PII redaction
- We offer two redaction layers: (a) pre-send client-side heuristics (customer-managed), and (b) server-side automated redaction hooks that remove tokens matching configured patterns (email, SSN, MRN).
- For hosted customers that opt-in to server-side redaction, outputs with redacted fields will still be storable but redaction placeholders will appear in persisted outputs and audit exports.
- Action: please share your sample schema (field list) and we’ll map patterns in the retention_matrix_v1.xlsx.

3) Audit exports and prompt text
- Hosted default: audit logs include request IDs, timestamps, model, token counts, and prompt hashes. Full prompt text is NOT included in long-term audit exports by default; it is available in short-lived diagnostics exports (rotated, 7-day retention) for debugging.
- Opt-out option: we can disable prompt-text in diagnostics exports per-tenant; doing so reduces visibility for debugging and incident forensics.

4) Evidence and artifacts
- Attached: retention_matrix_v1.xlsx (updated with explicit TTLs per category) and a redacted sample audit_export.csv showing the format (request_id, timestamp, model, token_count, prompt_hash).
- We will provide SOC2 artifact references and a sample log export as an NDA-backed package if required.

Next steps / mutual actions:
- CarePilot: send the PII field schema and confirm the one route that needs 30-day retention by EOD Friday.
- Redwood: we’ll update the retention matrix and provide a redacted audit export sample, plus a brief note on operational impacts of disabling prompt text in diagnostics.

If this looks good I can prepare a short security appendix you can attach to your procurement packet.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Security & Privacy, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
